title: שְׂאוּ לְבַבְכֶם לְכַפֵּיכֶם | Səū l'Vavkhem l'Khapeikhem, an ofan piyyuṭ for the Shabbat before Rosh haShanah by Rabbi Isaac ben Moses
author: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (transcription & naqdanut)

coauthors.name: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (transcription & naqdanut)
coauthors.bio: From a family of musicians, Isaac Gantwerk Mayer believes that creative art is one of the most powerful ways to get in touch with the divine. He composes music and poetry in Hebrew and English. (He also translates and authors his own original works.) Isaac runs a Jewish music transcription service, which will transcribe and set any Jewish music in any language, recorded or written. Contact his service on Facebook or via his music blog.

coauthors.name: Isaac ben Moses of Vienna
coauthors.bio: Isaac ben Moses of Vienna, also called Isaac Or Zarua or the RIAZ (fl. 13th c.), born in Bohemia, is considered to be one of the prominent rabbis of the Middle Ages. He attained his fame in Vienna and his major work, the halakhic guide known as the Or Zarua, a compilation of halakhic decisions and legal rulings, was very popular among Ashkenazic Jewry. He was a member of the Ḥasidei Ashkenaz and studied under many scholars, including Eliezer ben Joel HaLevi, Judah ben Samuel of Regensburg, Samson of Coucy and Eleazar of Worms. He was among the teachers of Meir of Rothenburg.

excerpt: This is the second piyyuṭ in a yotsrot cycle for the Shabbat before Rosh haShanah, according to Minhag Polin (as traditionally practiced in the Ashkenazi communities of northeastern Germany and Poland), all written by a Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Moshe haLevi according to the authorial acrostic. Zunz identifies the author as Rabbi Isaac ben Moses of Mainz, who died in the Gzerot Tatno of 1096. Fraenkel disputes this and suggests Rabbi Isaac ben Moses of Vienna (a/k/a the Or Zarua), of the Ḥasidei Ashkenaz, who died in around 1270. The ofan is an invocation to the listener to repent, calling upon specific angels by name. Also included is the German text of Isaac Seligman Baer's Avodat Yisrael translation, in modernized spelling.
content:
This is the second piyyuṭ in a yotsrot cycle for the Shabbat before Rosh haShanah, according to Minhag Polin (as traditionally practiced in the Ashkenazi communities of northeastern Germany and Poland), all written by a Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Moshe haLevi according to the authorial acrostic. Zunz identifies the author as Rabbi Isaac ben Moses of Mainz, who died in the Gzerot Tatno of 1096. Fraenkel disputes this and suggests Rabbi Isaac ben Moses of Vienna (a/k/a the Or Zarua), of the Ḥasidei Ashkenaz, who died in around 1270. The ofan piyyuṭ is an invocation to the listener to repent, calling upon specific angels by name. Also included is the German text of Isaac Seligman Baer’s Avodat Yisrael translation, in modernized spelling.
Source (Hebrew) Translation (English) Translation (German)
שְׂאוּ לְבַבְכֶם | לְכַפֵּיכֶם | וְרַחֲצוּ־נָא וְהִזַּֽכּוּ
וְהָסִֽירוּ | וְהַעֲבִֽירוּ | מֵרְאוֹת שָׁוְא וְהִדָּבְקוּ
בְּיִרְאַת אֵל | יִשְׂרָאֵל | יַשְּׁרוּ לֵב וְהַצְדִּֽיקוּ
בְּיוֹם כִּי בָא | חֲקֹר חוֹבָה | וְיֹֽשֶׁר לֵב וְגַם תִּזְכּוּ
וְהָֽבוּ עֹז | לְמֶֽלֶךְ עֹז | וְתִפְאֶֽרֶת בְּמִקְדָּשׁוֹ
רוֹמְמ֡וּ יְ֘הֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קׇדְשׁ֑וֹ׃ (תהלים צט:ט)
Raise your hearts in your hands, and pray wash and be cleansed,
and turn away and pass from foolish sights, and cling to revering the Deity!
Israel, set right your heart and be just
on the coming day, investigate guilt and righteous hearts and also merit
and grant might to the Sovereign of might and Their Temple’s glory.
Exalt the Cause our God and bow to Their holy mountain! (Psalms 99:9)
Erhebet euere Herzen samt euern Händen und waschet und reiniget euch!
Entfernt und schafft die Falschheit weg aus den Augen! Haltet an der Gottesfurcht, Israel!
Seid redlichen Herzens, auf dass ihr gerecht ausgehet am Tage, der da mahnt,
zur Untersuchung der Schuld und der Frömmigkeit, dass ihr, schuldlos gesprochen,
die Verherrlichung gebet dem Könige der Herrlichkeit und Pracht in seinem Heiligtume.
„Erhebet den Ewigen, unsern Gott, und werfet euch nieder auf seinem heiligen Berge!”
הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ | וְהַקְדִּֽישׁוּ | לְחַי יוֹשֵׁב עַל־כִּסֵּא
נָא תִּקְעוּ | וְהָרִֽיעוּ | בְּיוֹם חַגֵּֽנוּ כֵּֽסֶה
וְהֵחָרְדוּ | וְהִתְוַדּוּ | לְהָסִיר רֹֽעַ מַעֲשֶׂה
וְלֵב קִרְעוּ | וְהַדְמִֽיעוּ | פְּנֵי אֵל עָוֺן נוֹשֵׂא
כִּי עַל־כֹּל | יַעֲבִיר קוֹל | וְשִׁלַּם אֹתוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ
רוֹמְמ֡וּ יְ֘הֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קׇדְשׁ֑וֹ׃ (תהלים צט:ט)
Gather together and sanctify the Living One dwelling on a throne.
Pray blast a long blast and a tremulous blast on the covered day of our festival,
and quake and confess to turn away evil deeds,
and tear the heart and come to tears before the face of the Deity who bears iniquity,
for over all a voice will pass and fulfill their just deserts.
Exalt the Cause our God and bow to Their holy mountain! (Psalms 99:9)
Rüstet euch und heiliget den Lebendigen auf dem Throne Sitzenden;
blaset und stoßet in die Posaune an unserm festlichen Gerichtstage!
Gehet in euch und bekennet und entfernt die böse Tat!
Zerreißet das Herz und erstehet in Tränen den Allmächtigen, dass er die Sünde vergebe!
Denn über Alles lässt er das Urteil ergehen und vergilt dem Frevler nach seiner Tat.
„Erhebet den Ewigen, unsern Gott, und werfet euch nieder auf seinem heiligen Berge!”
יְׄרוֹמֵם צוּר | בְּלֵב עָצוּר | בִּקְרֹא מִקְרָא קֹֽדֶשׁ
צְׄמֹד חִנּוּן | וְגַם רִנּוּן | כְּשַׁי קָרֵב בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ
חֲׄפֹץ לִטְהָר | לֵב נִמְהָר | וְרֽוּחַ נָכוֹן חַדֵּשׁ
קְׄנֵה עַמָּךְ | בָּךְ נִתְמָךְ | פְּרֹשׁ בְּיִרְאָה וְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ
בַּׄרׄ לֵבָב | חֲשֹׁב נֶעֱלָב | כְּזֶֽבַח שַׁי בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ
בְּׄיׄוֹם יִקְרַב | עָוֺן רַב | בְּאֶחָד שְׁבִיעִי חֹֽדֶשׁ
מְׄשֹׁׄךְ חַסְדָּךְ | הֱׄיוֹת לְעַבְדָּךְ | רֽוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה לְחַדְּשׁוֹ
רוֹמְמ֡וּ יְ֘הֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קׇדְשׁ֑וֹ׃ (תהלים צט:ט)
Exalt the Rock with a steady heart, on calling the holy gathering.
Yoke together petition with cheering, like a gift to bring near in holiness.
Desire to purify an anxious heart, renew a prepared spirit!
Acquire Your people which is supported by You, distinguished in awe, and sanctify
the pure of heart; think of the crushed like a gift-offering in holiness
on the day of offering up great iniquity on the first of the seventh month.[1] Rosh haShanah, the first day of the seventh month. 
Extend Your mercy, that Your servants be renewed in a new spirit.
Exalt the Cause our God and bow to Their holy mountain! (Psalms 99:9)
Andächtigen Herzens erheben sie Dich, unser Hort, in heiliger Festversammlung,
verbindend Bitt- und Lobgebete, wie eine Gabe dargebracht im Heiligtum.
O möchtest Du sie reinigen die betörten Herzen und mit festem Sinn erneuern!
O nimm Dich Deines Volkes an, das auf Dich sich stützet und sich ganz der Gottesfurcht,
der Heiligung bestrebet. Das lautere, gebeugte Herz beachte gleich der Opfergabe im Heiligtum.
Und kommen am Ersten des siebenten Monates der Missetaten viele vor Dich,
o so neige Deine Gnade den Kindern Deiner Diener zu und erneuere ihnen einen neuen Geist!
„Erhebet den Ewigen, unsern Gott, und werfet euch nieder auf seinem heiligen Berge!”
בְּנֵי מַֽעֲלָה | בְּעֹז גְּדֻלָּה | מִיכָאֵל וְגַבְרִיאֵל
בְּעַד עַמְּכֶם | שְׂאוּ קוֹלְכֶם | בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב וְיִשְׂרָאֵל
עֲרֹךְ תְּפִלָּה | מְהֻלָּלָה | רְפָאֵל וַהֲדַרְנִיאֵל
וּשְׂרָפִים | לַאֲלָפִים | צְעֹק חֽוּשׁוּ לְעֻזִּיאֵל
וְהַחַיּוֹת | בְּכׇל־פִּיּוֹת | עֲרֹךְ תַּחַן לְמַלְכִּיאֵל
בְּנוֹת עִירוֹ | בְּרֹב הֲדָרוֹ | אֲשֶׁר עַמּוֹ לוֹ שׁוֹאֵל
וּנְפוֹצִים | נִקְבָּצִים | כְּמַאֲמָרוֹ יְמַלֵּא אֵל
עֲבֹר מַלְכָּם | בְּיוֹם חֻקָּם | וַיהֹוָה יֵלֵךְ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ
רוֹמְמ֡וּ יְ֘הֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קׇדְשׁ֑וֹ׃ (תהלים צט:ט)
O those of on high, in great might, Michael and Gabriel,
raise your voice for your people, the children of Jacob and Israel!
Array praised prayer, Raphael and Hadraniel,
and snake-angels for the thousands, shout out, hurry to Uzziel,[2] Or possibly, “the Deity, my strength.” In some manuscripts, written as two words rather than one. 
and living-angels, array with all mouths petition to Malkiel.[3] Or possibly, “the Deity, my Sovereign.” In some manuscripts, written as two words rather than one. 
Building Their city in Their great splendor is what Their people ask,
that the scattered be gathered to fulfill the word of the Deity.
Pass before them, their king,[4] The messiah, based on a rabbinic interpretation of Micah 2:13  on the day of their law; and the Cause will go at the head!
Exalt the Cause our God and bow to Their holy mountain! (Psalms 99:9)
Ihr mächtig großen Wesen der Höhe, Michael und Gabriel,
erhebet euere Stimme für Israel, euer Volk, die Söhne Jakobs!
Ordnet euer gerühmtes Gebet, Raphael und Hadarniel!
Ihr tausende Seraphim, eilet und flehet zu meinem starken Gotte!
ihr Chajoth, bringet mit vollem Munde die Bitte vor meinen mächtigen König,
dass er sein Volk erhöret, seine Stadt wieder erbauet in aller Pracht und die Zerstreuten dahin sammelt.
Es erfülle sein Wort der Herr und lasse vorausziehen den König am bestimmten Tage, und Er, der Ewige, an der Spitze.
„Erhebet den Ewigen, unsern Gott, und werfet euch nieder auf seinem heiligen Berge!”
בְּקוֹל יָרוֹן | מִטַּטְרוֹן | לִפְתֹּֽחַ בְּמֵישָׁרִים
זְכוּת אָבוֹת | וְאִמָּהוֹת | וְזֵֽכֶר חֶֽסֶד נְעוּרִים
וַהֲרוּגִים | וּשְׂרוּפִים | בְּאֵשׁ יוֹקֵד תַּבְעֵרִים
לְקִדּוּשׁ שֵׁם | מְאֹד וְנֶֽשֶׁם | בְּכׇל־כֹּחָם מִתְעוֹרְרִים
וְהַתּוֹרָה | הַטְּהוֹרָה | בְּפִי הָעָם נֶחְזָרִים
תִּתְעוֹדֵד | זְכוּת לְלַמֵּד | עֲלֵי הוֹגִים מְצֹעָרִים
בְּרֹב צָרוֹת | וּמַחֲסוֹרוֹת | אֲשֶׁר גּוֹלִים לְכׇל־שְׁעָרִים
שְׁפֹךְ תַּחֲנוּן | פְּנֵי חַנּוּן | לְפָאֵר מְקוֹם מִקְדָּשׁוֹ
רוֹמְמ֡וּ יְ֘הֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קׇדְשׁ֑וֹ׃ (תהלים צט:ט)
The Metatron will shout aloud to open straightaway
the merit of the patriarchs and matriarchs, the remembrance of the mercy of youth,
and the slain and burnt in burning igniting fire,
to sanctify the name with property and body,[5] Find Pesachim 25a and its interpretation of Deuteronomy 6:4  arousing with all their strength.
And the pure Teaching that is returned into the people’s mouth,
encourage merit to teach its matters to the afflicted
in many stresses and lackings, who are exiled to all the gates.
Spill out petition before the Merciful to glorify the place of Their temple!
Exalt the Cause our God and bow to Their holy mountain! (Psalms 99:9)
Es rufe laut Metatron und erwähne die Geradheit und das Verdienst der Altväter und Mütter.
Er erinnere an die Jugendtreue Israels, an die Gemordeten, Verbrannten, auf den brennenden Holzstoß Geworfenen,
die zur Heiligung des göttlichen Namens willig Gut und Blut hingaben.
Und die reine Lehre, geläufig dem Munde des Volkes,
auch sie mache sich auf zur Verteidigung ihrer gequälten Bekenner.
Die unter vielen Leiden und Entbehrungen überall hin Vertriebenen ergießen ihr Flehen
vor dem Allgnädigen, dass Er wieder verherrliche die Stätte seines Heiligtums.
„Erhebet den Ewigen, unsern Gott, und werfet euch nieder auf seinem heiligen Berge!”
